title: Draft: Add ILNP dissector (RFC 6740 - RFC 6748)
description: The Identifier-Locator Network Protocol (ILNP) is a network-layer protocol designed to enhance the scalability, flexibility, and mobility of the Internet.

notes.body:
This is a "counter proposal" to !20328.  I don't think we need to use as many "internal" structures as the original patch.  The main theme is pulling everything into packet-ilnp.c and having the IPv6 dissector explicitly call it when it reaches the ILNP Nonce Destination.

The main thing that needs to be figured out going forward is how to manage the ILNP addresses.  They shouldn't be part of all packet_info\* packets (because 99.9% of packets won't need them), but I'm not sure what "address layer" they should overwrite.  Currently they are not overwriting any of them and I still managed to achieve the same functionality (minus TCP/UDP, which we can discuss).

Thoughts welcome.

Great, I agree with the changes that have been made.

To answer you question about the address layer, The combination of the Locator (L64) and the Node Identifier (NID) form the Identifier-Locator Vector (I-LV) which is the network layer address. The Locator is the first 8 bytes which points to a dynamic Network location improved mobility/multi-homing over IPv6 and the NID is the second 8 bytes which points to a static device address on the network. However, for transport layer state, only the Identifier is relevant because it is the only static component. I think for TCP/UDP with ILNP, pinfo->src and pinfo->dst can be set to the ILNP src/dst NIDs during the ILNP dissector. Though I am unsure about the checksum verification. The only difference between ILNP and IPv6 checksum verification for TCP/UDP is that in ILNP, the Locator is zeroed before calculation since it is dynamic. Otherwise, the calculation is the same.

Please let me know what you think.
